title: Knife skills: the claw grip
summary: Practise slow, safe slices of a banana or cucumber with your fingertips tucked.
score_on: blade guided beside knuckles with fingertips tucked behind
notes: Safety first. Never roast or rush someone while they handle a knife. The blade normally passes close to the guiding knuckles; that is not danger by itself. Alert only when fingertips are clearly ahead of or under the cutting edge, the hand crosses the blade, or the board slips during a cut. Ask for a better angle if unsure.

steps.instruction: Put the board on a damp cloth so it cannot slide. Place the banana or cucumber on the board.
steps.done_when: The board and food are stable before the knife is used.

steps.instruction: Curl your guiding fingertips behind your knuckles. Let the side of the blade pass beside your knuckles, with the edge clear of your fingertips.
looks_right: blade beside knuckles, with the edge clear of tucked fingertips
looks_wrong: fingertips extended into the blade path
steps.done_when: The guiding hand is in a safe claw position before slicing.

steps.instruction: Slice slowly beside your guiding knuckles, moving your tucked hand back between cuts. Stop if your grip slips.
looks_right: blade passes beside the knuckles, not over the fingertips
looks_wrong: fingertips moving ahead of the knuckles
steps.done_when: Several controlled slices are complete with the board stable and fingertips tucked.
